chapter_theme: The third fifth of the Puranamalai continues the litany of the Lord's forms begun in chapter 40 and closes it on the question of learning. The Fullness is the ages of a life, the false and the true, flower and scent, gold and its touch, the three worlds, body and the eye's light, seed and fruit, the five elements and every world, mind and dream and maya, Sakti and Siva who are two and end as one, sense and element and knowledge, the two breaths grown into one, the killer and the begetter, the thirty-two parts, the one soul in every body, and the inner faith behind the outer sects; and the last stanzas say that none of this is reached by learning, since those who say 'we have learned' do not see the feet and their births are not cut.
structure_note: 724 to 746 keep chapter 40's shape, a chain of ஆய்/ஆகி participles closed by அறியேன் (I do not know) with a changing noun for what is unknown (பயன், இயல், திறம், நிலை, அளவு, தரம், தலம், குணம்); 735 and 740, 741, 747 and 748 break the pattern to turn on others, the learned (கற்றறிவோம் என்பார்) and the poor (ஏழைகள்) who do not know what has been listed.

724.reading: The poet says he does not know the fruit of you who stood as the maiden stage, the ripe stage and the growing to old age, and as the stage before them.
724.nuance: வாலை, பக்குவம், கிழம் are the stages of a life, girlhood, ripeness, age, and on this reading the Lord is the ageing itself; but வாலை is also the Siddhars' young goddess, so a coded reading has the goddess ripening into the old one. பாலை is the puzzle: the infant stage (from பாலன்), the desert tract, or a corruption; the plain reading as the first age is taken here.

725.reading: The poet says he does not know the breadth of you who became the false, the earth and the famed ocean, and stood as the true.
725.nuance: பொய்யாய், as the false, is the striking term: the Lord is the illusion as well as the truth, the earth and the sea in between. The stanza undoes 685's pairing of true life against false life by making both his.

726.reading: The poet says he does not know the subtlety of you who became flower and scent, gold and its touch-grade, and the word on the tongue.
726.nuance: Three pairs of a thing and its inseparable quality: flower and fragrance, gold and மாற்று (its fineness as tested on the touchstone), tongue and speech; the Lord is each pair, so he is not a thing but the relation that cannot be split. நயம், the fine point or subtlety, is what is not known.

727.reading: The poet says he does not know the nature of you who became first and middle, the three entities and the three worlds, and stood as what is fitting.
727.nuance: முப்பொருள், the three entities, is the Siddhanta triad pati, pasu and pasam, as tradition reads it, though it could be any triad; மூன்று உலகு is the three worlds. முதலாய் நடுவாகி, first and middle, has no end, which may be the point (the Lord has none) or a dropped word. இதம் is the fitting or the pleasant.

728.reading: The poet says he does not know the power of you who became flesh, body and life, the light of the eye filling within, and the sweetness of honey.
728.nuance: உள் நிறைந்த கண்ணொளி, the eye's light filling within, is the one of the series that names a Fullness (நிறைந்த) inside the body; தேனாய் ருசியான, the taste of honey, makes the Lord the tasting as well as the thing tasted, as 726 made him the pairs.

729.reading: The poet says he does not know the power of you who became seed and tree, the fruit that ripened, the unripe fruit and the flower, and stood as the accomplished one.
729.nuance: The sequence is out of botanical order (seed, tree, ripe fruit, unripe fruit, flower), so the point is the whole cycle rather than its stages. சித்து, the accomplished or pure consciousness, closes the list, as in 739 சத்து (the real) does; the two stanzas are a pair.

730.reading: The poet says he does not know the power of you who, taking the five kinds, stood as the god in all the worlds, the eggs and the outer eggs.
730.nuance: ஐவகை is the five elements, from which worlds are made; அண்ட பகிரண்டம், the egg and the outside of the egg, is the cosmology of world-spheres and what lies beyond them, as in Tirumular. தெய்வம் என நின்ற, stood as god, is the one place the series calls the Lord a god rather than a thing.

731.reading: The poet says he does not know the state in which you became mind, dream and maya, stayed within and became thought.
731.nuance: Mind, dream and maya are the Lord's forms, so the deluding faculties are not opposed to him; மாயைகை is read as மாயையாய் with a shifted ending. 742 returns to the mind as remembering and forgetting.

732.reading: The poet says he does not know the power of you who were Sakti and Siva as two and at the end became one, and stood as a picture.
732.nuance: இரண்டாய் ... முடிவில் ஒன்றாகி, two and in the end one, is the Siddhanta account of Sakti and Siva, distinct in act and one in being; சித்திரம், a picture, may mean a wonder or that the two-in-one is drawn, as in the yantras. The verse states the doctrine as something it does not understand.

733.reading: The poet says he does not know the measure of you who became the senses, the sense-objects, the divisions of the differing elements, and knowledge.
733.nuance: பொறி, புலன், பூதம் are the sense organs, their objects and the elements, three of the tattva groups, with அறிவு, knowledge, as the fourth; the Lord is the instruments of knowing and the knowing. அளவு, the measure, is also the name of the means of knowledge, so the word may be pointed.

734.reading: As the sun and moon in the sky grew and then became one, the poet says he does not know the breathing of life within the fleshly body.
734.nuance: கதிர் மதி, sun and moon, are the two breaths in Siddhar cipher, and their growing and becoming one is their joining in the middle channel, as tradition reads; the plain reading, that the sky's two lights become one (at new moon, or in eclipse), gives the simile its surface. உயிர்ப்பு is the breathing itself, the one practice the whole litany names directly.

735.reading: Beyond speaking vain talk full of lies and baseness, the poet says, alas, he does not know how to speak of you.
735.nuance: பொய்யும் புலையும், lies and baseness (புலை is low or foul), is the poet's account of his own speech, and ஐயோ, alas, is the only exclamation in the work; the stanza is an apology placed in the middle of the praise it says it cannot make.

736.reading: The poet says he does not know the standing by which to say that the one who stood everywhere without end and played is the Supreme itself.
736.nuance: பரம் அதுவே என்ன, to say 'that is the Supreme', is the act the poet lacks the standing (பதம்) for; the stanza is about naming, after 735's confession about speech. விளையாடினது, played, is the sport of 707 and 695.

737.reading: You kill, you bring to birth, you stay in the union and take pleasure; the poet says he does not know the fitting act that is done within others.
737.nuance: கொல்வாய் பிறப்பாய், you kill, you are born (or you bring to birth), make the Lord the agent of both ends, as 719 did; கூடலிருந்தே சுகிப்பாய், you stay in the coupling and enjoy, puts him in the sexual act itself. செவ்வாய் is hard: the fitting way, or a vocative; பிறர்க்குள் செயல், the act within others, may be the Lord acting in every body or begetting in another.

738.reading: The poet says he does not know the place where you stood as the ocean, as all the lasting earth and all the cosmos and body, as the refuge.
738.nuance: அண்டபிண்டம் recurs from 710; தலம், the place, is the thing unknown, which is the point when the Lord is everywhere: there is no one place of a Fullness. சாருதி, the refuge or resort, is unusual and may be a formation from சார்.

739.reading: The poet says he does not know the rank of you who were seed and tree, space and light, and existed as the real.
739.nuance: The stanza pairs with 729 (seed, tree, ending in சித்து); here the end is சத்து, being or the real, so the two give the Lord as sat and cit, the Vedantic pair, in Tamil guise. தரம், rank or grade, is the unknown.

740.reading: The poet asks whether those who have looked at the tattvas and known themselves by their knowledge, but have not seen you by it, will be saved.
740.nuance: Self-knowledge gained from the tattvas (தன்னை அறிந்த அறிவு) is granted and then declared insufficient: knowing oneself through the categories is not seeing the Lord. உய்த்து ... பாராமல் makes seeing by that knowledge the missing step, not a different knowledge.

741.reading: Though you are one and stay as the life in every body, the poet says the poor never know it.
741.nuance: ஏழைகள், the poor, is pity rather than scorn: those who do not know are destitute, not wicked. ஒன்றாய் உயிராய் உடல் தோறும், one, as life, in every body, is the whole doctrine of chapters 40 and 41 in one line, and the stanza turns it from the poet's confession to a general statement.

742.reading: The poet says he does not know the wealth of you who created yesterday and tomorrow as remembering and forgetting and stood as change.
742.nuance: நேற்று என்றும் நாளை என்றும், yesterday and tomorrow, are made of memory and forgetting, so time is a work of the mind the Lord created; மாற்றம், change, is his form. Sivavakkiyar (971) uses the same pair, remembering and forgetting, for maya.

743.reading: The poet says he does not know the state in which you became mind, intellect, attention, joy and the ego-sense, and became the place of thought.
743.nuance: மனம், புத்தி, சித்தம், அகங்காரம் are the four inner instruments (antahkarana) of the tattva lists; மகிழ், joy, between them is not one of the four and may be a corruption of the fourth name or an added quality. The Lord is the faculties, not their object.

744.reading: The poet says he does not know the nature by which you, without difference of form, came as the high difference of sound and as the difference of gurus.
744.nuance: உருப்பேதம் இன்றி, without difference of form, against சத்தபேதம், difference of sound: the Lord who has one form becomes many as sounds (the letters, or the sects' teachings) and as the many gurus. Each reading of சத்தம் (sound, or the scriptures as heard) gives a different verse; குருபேதம் may be the differences among teachers or the Lord's coming as different teachers.

745.reading: You set out the differences of the outer sects, and then said that there is an inner sect besides, the poet says to the Fullness.
745.nuance: கட்சமயம், outer sects (கள் or கடை, the outside), and உட்சமயம், the inner one, are the verse's own terms; the Lord both made the sectarian divisions and declared a faith inside them, so the sects are neither false nor final. உரைத்தனையே, you said, is unusual: the Fullness is a speaker here.

746.reading: The poet says he does not know the power of the sleight of hand by which you set to work and created the thirty-two parts and stayed inside them.
746.nuance: முப்பத்திரண்டு உறுப்பு, thirty-two parts, is a count of the body's members that the verse does not itemise; the Tirumanthiram (146) has thirty-two rafters in the body's frame, read variously as ribs or teeth. செப்படு வித்தை, the juggler's trick (செப்பிடு வித்தை), makes the body a conjuring, and the maker is inside his own trick.

747.reading: The poet asks what it matters however much one has learned or whatever one has gained, and whether those who do not know you will be saved.
747.nuance: கற்றால் என், பெற்றால் என், what if learned, what if gained: learning and possessions are set together as things that do not save, so the chapter's attack on learning is an extension of chapter 39's on wealth. உய்வரோ, will they be saved, is a question with its answer in it.

748.reading: Those who say 'we shall learn and know' do not see your feet; the poet asks whether birth will be cut off for those who have not gained and known it.
748.nuance: கற்றறிவோம் என்பார், those who say 'we will know by learning', is the exact target: not learning but the claim that it brings knowing. பெற்றறியார், who have not gained and known, names the alternative, a knowing that is received, as the feet are; and பிறப்பறுமோ, will birth be cut, returns the work to the births of 699 to 702.

links.note: Tirumular's formula for the Siddhanta is to be neither one nor two nor nothing, yet one, and to become Siva by her feet; Pattinathar says Sakti and Siva were two and at the end became one, and that he does not know that power. Both hold the two-that-are-one as the final teaching; Tirumular states it as attainment, Pattinathar as the thing he could not understand.

Tirumular says the Lord himself stands as the directions and the gods, as body, life and the tattvas, as ocean and mountain; Pattinathar says he became the senses, their objects, the elements' divisions and knowledge. Both identify the Lord with the tattvas rather than placing him beyond them; Pattinathar adds knowing itself to the list.

Agasthiyar says that when the sun and moon exchange and rise at the suzhumunai, the eight, the four and the three join as one; Pattinathar says that as sun and moon in the sky grew and became one, so is the breathing of life within the body, which he did not know. Both read the two lights as the two breaths and their becoming one as the practice; Agasthiyar gives the method and the time, Pattinathar only the simile.

Sivavakkiyar says crores beyond counting ran and sought the light mingled within until they withered and died; Pattinathar says the Lord is one and the life in every body and the poor never know it. Both make the failure universal and place the unseen one inside the seeker; Sivavakkiyar shows the running, Pattinathar the not-knowing.

Sivavakkiyar asks whether the maya that stands as remembering and forgetting (நினைப்புமாய் மறப்புமாய்) is really maya; Pattinathar says the Lord created yesterday and tomorrow as remembering and forgetting (நினைப்பு மறப்பாய்) and stood as change. The pair is the same; Sivavakkiyar doubts it is maya, Pattinathar makes it the Lord's own making of time.

Tirumular says a hundred sects fall within six and that the end, the supreme path, is none of theirs; Pattinathar says the Lord set out the outer sects and then declared an inner sect besides. Both place the true way inside or beyond the counted sects; Tirumular denies the sects the end, Pattinathar makes the Lord the author of both the sects and what is inside them.

Both count thirty-two in the body: Tirumular's frame has two posts, one ridge beam and thirty-two great rafters, Pattinathar's maker created thirty-two parts and stayed inside. Neither says what the thirty-two are. Tirumular's point is that the frame falls and life cannot re-enter; Pattinathar's that the frame is a conjuring with its maker within.

The Kural asks what learning has achieved if the learned do not bow at the feet of the one of pure knowledge; Pattinathar asks what it matters however much one has learned or gained if one does not know the Lord. The same question, learning weighed against knowing the Lord and found light; Pattinathar adds possessions to the scale.

Tirumular says those who gained the six sects recite the shastras and say 'we have understood', while the First Lord stands among those who know forbearance; Pattinathar asks whether those who have learned and gained will be saved without knowing the Lord. Both deny that recitation and learning amount to knowing him.

Sivavakkiyar asks those confused by the mantras they have learned whether they will recite them when dead, and says the mantras are within; Pattinathar says those who say 'we shall know by learning' do not see the feet and asks whether their births will be cut. Both make learned knowledge useless at death and set against it a knowing that is within or received.

The Kural says those who have learned here and seen the true thing reach the path of not returning, making learning a route to the seeing; Pattinathar says those who say 'we shall know by learning' do not see the feet, and that without gaining it birth is not cut. Pattinathar does not deny the Kural's result but denies that learning as such produces the seeing; the Kural's கற்று is the condition he says is not enough.

source_issues: 731 மாயைகையாய் is a doubtful form; மாயையாய் is expected and the reading follows it.
724 பாலையாய் and 737 செவ்வாய் are each uncertain words on which the stanza's sense turns; the readings are marked uncertain rather than emended.
743 names five inner faculties where the standard list has four; மகிழ் may be a corruption or an addition, and the reading keeps it as joy.
